surfaces.part: packed earth ground patch with soot marks, ash and embers

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64x48 rectangle (width 64 on every row) of speckled brown earth viewed straight down. Dark soot spots with grey ash and red ember pixels sit at rows 3-11, 19-27 and 35-43, plus a few charred stick pixels near rows 38-43. The column scans show no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical face anywhere. There is no front face, so this is a flat ground decal, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a packed-earth ground patch, so the grass and paving references are the right kind. The soil carries grain and speckle in about 4-5 brown steps. The soot bursts are drawn in tinted dark browns with warm ember dots, not a neutral black line, and the measured 0% neutral dark-edge share confirms this. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. It has 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7), so density is acceptable but a little under the best references. The total of 13 raw colours is thin next to the 80-colour grass, and the soil ramp is shallower than a reference material. The scattered small bursts also read less clearly than a single ash star, but that is an object-fidelity matter and not a style failure. A careful artist would accept it next to the references, so it passes narrowly.
